chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Ubayd Allah informed us from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad, from al-Ala', from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
When a man travels during Ramadan, he should not approach women during the day in Ramadan, for that is forbidden for him.
ai.seo_question: Is a fasting traveler allowed to have intercourse during the day in Ramadan?
ai.summary: In al-Isfabar, Shaykh al-Tusi records this ruling from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), clarifying that for a traveler who has chosen to fast, sexual intercourse during daylight hours is strictly prohibited and invalidates the fast, mirroring the ruling for those at home. This highlights the Shia scholarly distinction between the permissibility of breaking the fast while traveling versus the specific prohibition of marital relations during the fasting hours, even for the traveler. The hadith underscores the sanctity of the fasting period's daylight hours regardless of one's travel status.
